nodes.label: determine whether the termination complies with the required written form, approved landlord form, required form content, and separate service requirements
nodes.why: These propositions prescribe writing, an approved form, specified form information, and separate service where applicable.

nodes.label: termination is void
nodes.why: A termination that does not comply with Articles 266l–266n is void.

nodes.label: request justification for the termination
nodes.why: The landlord's duty to justify is triggered when the tenant requests justification.

nodes.label: provide justification for the termination upon request
nodes.why: The propositions require the termination to be justified upon request.

nodes.label: determine whether the termination violates the principle of good faith
nodes.why: A termination is contestable if it violates the principle of good faith.

nodes.label: determine whether the landlord terminated because the tenant asserted tenancy claims in good faith
nodes.why: A landlord termination issued for that reason is contestable.

nodes.label: termination is contestable
nodes.why: The propositions identify good-faith violations and specified retaliatory terminations as grounds of contestability.

nodes.label: submit a request challenging the termination to the conciliation authority
nodes.why: A party intending to challenge must submit the request within the stated period, and the procedure is initiated by a conciliation request.

nodes.label: determine whether extension is excluded by the termination ground or equivalent replacement offer
nodes.why: The propositions exclude extension for specified termination grounds and generally where an equivalent replacement is offered.

nodes.label: extension is excluded
nodes.why: These provisions expressly exclude or generally exclude an extension in the stated circumstances.

nodes.label: submit a request for extension to the conciliation authority
nodes.why: A tenant may seek an extension and must submit that request to the conciliation authority.

nodes.label: determine whether termination causes unjustified hardship to the tenant or the tenant's family
nodes.why: Extension depends on hardship that cannot be justified by the landlord's interests.

nodes.label: weigh the tenant's hardship against the landlord's interests using the specified circumstances
nodes.why: The competent authority must consider the listed contractual, personal, need-based, and market circumstances in weighing interests.

nodes.label: determine whether the tenant did everything reasonably expected to avert hardship for a second extension
nodes.why: For a second extension request, the authority must also consider the tenant's reasonable efforts to avert hardship.

nodes.label: determine permitted extension duration, number of extensions, and any contract adaptation
nodes.why: The propositions set residential and business maximums, permit one or two extensions, except agreed extensions from the maximum, and allow adaptation to changed circumstances.

nodes.label: extension is granted on determined terms
nodes.why: An extension may be granted where the hardship standard is met, subject to the stated duration and number rules.

nodes.label: determine whether conciliation is omitted or validly waived
nodes.why: The propositions enumerate omitted proceedings and conditions for joint or unilateral waiver.

nodes.label: serve the request, summon the parties, and attempt informal conciliation
nodes.why: Conciliation precedes decision proceedings unless omitted, and the authority must serve, summon, and attempt reconciliation.

nodes.label: determine whether the claimant is in default at conciliation
nodes.why: Claimant default causes the request to be deemed withdrawn and the proceedings to be struck off.

nodes.label: conciliation request is deemed withdrawn and proceedings are struck off
nodes.why: The stated consequence follows if the claimant is in default.

nodes.label: determine whether an agreement, acknowledgment, or unconditional withdrawal is reached
nodes.why: The authority's recording duties differ depending on whether agreement is reached.

nodes.label: record and sign settlement, acknowledgment, or unconditional withdrawal and distribute minutes
nodes.why: The authority must record and obtain signatures, parties receive copies, and the recorded outcome has final and binding effect.

nodes.label: determine whether the conciliation authority submits a proposed decision
nodes.why: A proposed decision may be submitted in covered residential or commercial lease disputes affecting protection against termination or extension.

nodes.label: determine whether a party rejects the proposed decision within 20 days
nodes.why: Absent a timely rejection, the proposed decision is deemed accepted and final.

nodes.label: proposed decision is deemed accepted and final
nodes.why: A proposed decision is final if unchallenged within 20 days or if a timely action is not filed after rejection.

nodes.label: record lack of agreement and issue authorization to sue
nodes.why: If no agreement is reached, the authority must record that fact and issue authorization to sue to the claimant, including after rejection in covered proposed-decision matters.

nodes.label: file action with the court at the location of the immovable property
nodes.why: Authorization entitles court action after opening, the lease-dispute action period is 30 days, and the court at the property's location has jurisdiction.

transitions.condition: the termination does not comply with Articles 266l–266n
conciliation is not omitted or waived
hardship and landlord interests must be weighed
the hardship is not justified by the landlord's interests
an extension is granted within the applicable terms
the claimant is not in default
an agreement, acknowledgment, or unconditional withdrawal is reached
no party rejects within 20 days of written notification
a party rejects the proposed decision

deadlines.period: within 30 days for an indefinite tenancy
deadlines.runs_from: after receipt of the notice of termination
before the end of the contractual term for a fixed-term tenancy
written notification of the proposed decision
after the opening of the authorization to bring an action

deadlines.period: 30 days in disputes arising from residential and commercial lease and tenancy

obligations.party: landlord and tenant of residential and commercial premises
obligations.statement: Give notice of termination in writing.
Use a canton-approved termination form that states how the tenant may challenge termination or request extension and identifies the leased object.
Serve landlord termination separately on the tenant and the tenant's spouse or registered partner.
Submit the challenge request within 30 days after receipt of termination.
Submit an extension request to the conciliation authority within the deadline applicable to the tenancy term.
Take into account the specified contractual circumstances, tenancy duration, party circumstances and conduct, landlord own need and urgency, and local market conditions.
Also consider whether the tenant did everything reasonably expected to avert hardship.
Identify the opposing party, legal relief sought, and subject matter of the dispute in the request.
Serve the request without delay, simultaneously summon the parties, and attempt reconciliation in informal negotiations.
Appear in person at the conciliation hearing, subject to the stated exceptions.
Record the settlement, acknowledgment, or unconditional withdrawal in the minutes and have the parties sign it.
Receive one copy of the minutes.
Record lack of agreement in the minutes and issue authorization to sue.
Attach the authorization to bring the action or a declaration that conciliation is waived, available evidentiary documents, and a power of attorney where represented.

unsupported_gaps.what_is_missing: The propositions do not state the decision or remedy that follows a finding that a termination is contestable.
unsupported_gaps.why_it_matters: They establish contestability standards but do not specify whether the termination is annulled or what other relief is granted.

unsupported_gaps.what_is_missing: The propositions do not state the precise relationship between the three-month authorization period and the 30-day action period for residential and commercial lease disputes.
unsupported_gaps.why_it_matters: Both periods are supplied for court action, but the sources do not resolve which controls in this case.

unsupported_gaps.what_is_missing: The propositions refer to Article 271a paragraph 1 letters d and e but do not provide their substantive contestability standards.
unsupported_gaps.why_it_matters: The supplied exception cannot be applied to those unidentified underlying grounds.

scope: a tenant who has received a termination of a residential or commercial lease and is considering challenging it as void, abusive or improperly served, or requesting an extension
